\
The main goal of the __InNOutBT__ package is to readily create input data and
process output data for Meade & Pagel's (2022) [BayesTraits](https://www.evolution.reading.ac.uk/BayesTraitsV5.0.3/BayesTraitsV5.0.3.html) 
program.\

Here in this article, we show how to use __InNOutBT__'s function `shell.phyreg.proj`
for a full shell script run and log processing of multiple phylogenetic regression 
analyses with Meade & Pagel's (2022) [BayesTraits](https://www.evolution.reading.ac.uk/BayesTraitsV5.0.3/BayesTraitsV5.0.3.html) 
program. By reporting a directory path and the computer's operating system 
("unix" or "windows"), this function creates the project folder __BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project__
with associated example scripts.\

The available example of a shell script in Unix or Windows PowerShell helps to 
fully automate both the complete BayesTraits regression analyses and the processing 
of the resulting log and stones files, by automatically running the three main 
__InNOutBT__ functions `phyreg.inputs`, `phyreg.shell`, and `phyreg.outputs`, 
without directly opening the R or RStudio programs.\

Note that the __BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project__ folder that comes with __InNOutBT__ 
package was originally used in our recently published specific study on the ecological 
diversification of the Vataireoid legumes. So, you will have to edit the folder 
paths and analysis parameters in these example scripts according to your desired 
regression analyses. See the associated articles on how to set the parameters to 
[create input files](https://dboslab.github.io/InNOutBT/articles/phyreg_inputs.html)
with `phyreg.inputs` for the phylogenetic regression analyses, as well as to 
[create the internal shell script](https://dboslab.github.io/InNOutBT/articles/phyreg_shell.html) 
with `phyreg.shell` for the actual BayesTraits runs, and to 
[process the resulting output files](https://dboslab.github.io/InNOutBT/articles/phyreg_outputs.html)
with `phyreg.outputs`. You might also want to see the [BayesTraits 5.0.3 Manual](https://www.evolution.reading.ac.uk/BayesTraitsV5.0.3/Files/BayesTraitsV5.0.2-Manual.pdf)
for further details on each of BayesTraits parameters available for phylogenetic
regressions so as to better understand how to set the arguments available in the
__InNOutBT__ functions.\
\

# Setup

__InNOutBT__ is not on CRAN yet, but you can install the latest development version 
from [GitHub](https://github.com/):

``` r
#install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("DBOSlab/InNOutBT")
```
```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(InNOutBT)
```
\

# Creating a Unix shell project folder

The `shell.phyreg.proj` function is very simple and has only two arguments. By just 
setting any path on your computer and the argument `syst = "unix"`, you can readily
create the project folder __BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project__ with associated 
example files (R scripts, shell script, and data folder) for running the phylogenetic
regressions of the Vataireoid legumes on macOS Monterey. But then you can easily 
modify such available scripts for your specific analyses.\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(InNOutBT)

shell.phyreg.proj(dir_create_proj = "/Users/domingoscardoso",
                  syst = "unix")
```

After running the `shell.phyreg.proj` function, it will readily create the project folder __BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project__, a data folder with the input data files 
__vataireoids_1610_25May2022_BayesTraits.csv__ and __vatcomb30_24May22_Yule.con.tree__,
as well as the main shell script __BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh__ and R 
scripts __1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R__, __2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R__,
and __3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R__.\
\
```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/unix_shell_project.png", dpi = 300)
```
\
\
You should see the associated articles on how to set the parameters to 
[create input files](https://dboslab.github.io/InNOutBT/articles/phyreg_inputs.html)
with `phyreg.inputs` for the phylogenetic regression analyses, as well as to 
[create the internal shell script](https://dboslab.github.io/InNOutBT/articles/phyreg_shell.html) 
with `phyreg.shell` for the actual BayesTraits runs, and to 
[process the resulting output files](https://dboslab.github.io/InNOutBT/articles/phyreg_outputs.html)
with `phyreg.outputs`. In these articles, you will find how to fully edit the R 
scripts __1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R__, __2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R__,
and __3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R__ according to your particular study.
Otherwise, if you run the example files with the same parameter settings, you will 
be able to fully reproduce the analysis of our Vataireoid legume study.\

The main shell script file __BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh__ performs the
full phylogenetic regression analysis and processing of results. Its first lines
hold the paths to your folders, as shown in the image below, which you will set in
the next section. The path in the image is an example from an earlier version of
BayesTraits, so yours will be different.\
\
```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/unix_shell_project_script.png", dpi = 300)
```
\
\

# Running the Unix shell script 

You will work with two folders: the project folder __BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project__
and the folder where the BayesTraits executable file is installed. You always start
the analysis from the __project folder__. You do not need to open the BayesTraits
folder, because the main shell script moves there by itself to run the analyses,
and then brings the results back to the project folder.\

## Before the first run

__1.__ Download and install [BayesTraits](https://www.evolution.reading.ac.uk/BayesTraitsV5.0.3/BayesTraitsV5.0.3.html)
in any folder. Note the path to that folder and the name of the executable file,
such as __BayesTraitsV5__.\

__2.__ Check that the executable file starts, by running its full path in the Terminal.
If it starts and keeps waiting, press Control + C to leave it.

``` bash
/Users/yourname/BayesTraits/BayesTraitsV5
```

If macOS stops the program, for instance with the message __killed__ or a warning
that it cannot be opened, this is because macOS blocks programs downloaded from the
internet that are not signed. If you trust the source of the download, remove
the block with the following line, and then check again:

``` bash
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Users/yourname/BayesTraits/BayesTraitsV5
```

__3.__ Check that __InNOutBT__ and __treeio__ are installed in R. The package
__treeio__ is used to read the tree in the first R script and is available from
[Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org/packages/treeio/):

``` r
#install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("treeio")
```

__4.__ Check in the Terminal that __pandoc__ is available, because it is needed to write
the Word table. If the following line returns `FALSE`, [install pandoc](https://pandoc.org/installing.html):

``` bash
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::pandoc_available()'
```

## Editing the project files

Open each of the following files in any text editor, such as RStudio.\

__5.__ In the main shell script __BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh__, set:\

- __PROJECTFOLDER__: the path to the project folder;
- __BAYESTRFOLDER__: the path to the __folder__ that contains the BayesTraits
executable file, not the path to the file itself;
- __EMAIL__: your e-mail address, to receive a message when the analyses start and
finish. This depends on your computer being set up to send e-mail with the `mail`
command, but the analyses will run even if the message is not sent.

``` bash
PROJECTFOLDER="/Users/yourname/BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project"
BAYESTRFOLDER="/Users/yourname/BayesTraits"
EMAIL="your.address@example.com"
```

__6.__ In the R script __2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R__, set the same
BayesTraits folder again, as well as the name of the executable file. Both paths
to the BayesTraits folder must be identical:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
BayesTraits_dir = "/Users/yourname/BayesTraits",
BayesTraits_exe = "BayesTraitsV5",
```

__7.__ For your own study, also edit the three numbered R scripts as described in the
articles mentioned above, and replace the files in the __Data__ folder. To check
that everything works before a long analysis, you can first set a few iterations in
__2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R__, such as `bi = "2000"`, `it = "12000"`,
`sa = "500"`, and `st = c("10", "200")`. These values are only for testing, so set
your final values again before the real analysis.\

## Running the analysis

__8.__ Open the Terminal and move to the project folder:

``` bash
cd /Users/yourname/BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project
```

__9.__ Allow the main shell script to run. You need to do this only once:

``` bash
chmod 777 BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh
```

__10.__ Start the full analysis:

``` bash
./BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh
```

Keep the Terminal open and the computer awake until the script finishes. With the
number of iterations in the example scripts, this can take a long time.\

## What the script does

The main shell script then performs the following steps, with no further action from you:\

__1.__ Runs __1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R__, which saves the input files
in the folder __results_BayesTraits_phyreg_input__;\

__2.__ Runs __2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R__, which saves the run commands in
the folder __results_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell__ and copies them to the BayesTraits
folder, with the data and tree files;\

__3.__ Moves to the BayesTraits folder and runs all the analyses, removing the copied
files at the end;\

__4.__ Moves the results to the folders __BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs_log_stone__ and
__BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs_sch_trees__ in the project folder;\

__5.__ Runs __3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R__, which saves the final table
and the heatmaps in the folder __results_BayesTraits_phyreg_output__, within a
subfolder named with the current date, and opens these files.\

## If something goes wrong

The script continues after an error, so one problem can produce many messages. Look
at the __first__ error in the Terminal, because the later ones are often just consequences.\

| Message | Likely cause and solution |
|:----------------|:----------------------|
| `chmod: BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_unix.sh: No such file or directory` | You are not in the project folder. Repeat step 8. |
| `cannot open file '.../run_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell_unix.sh'` | `BayesTraits_dir` is wrong in __2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R__. See step 6. |
| `cd: no such file or directory` | `BAYESTRFOLDER` is wrong in the main shell script. See step 5. |
| `killed`, or many `mv: rename ...Log.txt ...: No such file or directory` messages | BayesTraits did not run. macOS may have blocked it (step 2), or `BayesTraits_exe` is wrong (step 6). |
| `Error in combinat::combn(fnames, 2) : n < m` | There are no results to process, because BayesTraits did not run. Solve the first error shown. |
\
\

# Creating a Windows PowerShell project folder

In the `shell.phyreg.proj` function, you can set any path on your PC and the argument
`syst = "windows"` to readily create the project folder __BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project__ 
with associated example files (R scripts, PowerShell script, and data folder) for running
the phylogenetic regressions of the Vataireoid legumes on a Windows PC. But then you 
can easily modify such available scripts for your specific analyses.\

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(InNOutBT)

shell.phyreg.proj(dir_create_proj = "C:/Users/Matt_/Documents",
                  syst = "windows")
```

After running the `shell.phyreg.proj` function, it will readily create the project folder __BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project__, a data folder with the input data files 
__vataireoids_1610_25May2022_BayesTraits.csv__ and __vatcomb30_24May22_Yule.con.tree__,
as well as the main PowerShell script __BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1__ 
and R scripts __1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R__, __2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R__,
and __3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R__.\
\
```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/windows_shell_project.png", dpi = 300)
```
\
\
You should see the associated articles on how to set the parameters to 
[create input files](https://dboslab.github.io/InNOutBT/articles/phyreg_inputs.html)
with `phyreg.inputs` for the phylogenetic regression analyses, as well as to 
[create the internal shell script](https://dboslab.github.io/InNOutBT/articles/phyreg_shell.html) 
with `phyreg.shell` for the actual BayesTraits runs, and to 
[process the resulting output files](https://dboslab.github.io/InNOutBT/articles/phyreg_outputs.html)
with `phyreg.outputs`. In these articles, you will find how to fully edit the R 
scripts __1_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_inputs.R__, __2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R__,
and __3_processing_BayesTraits_phyreg_outputs.R__ according to your particular study.
Otherwise, if you run the example files with the same parameter settings, you will 
be able to fully reproduce the analysis of our Vataireoid legume study.\

The main PowerShell script file __BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1__ performs
the full phylogenetic regression analyses and processing of results. Its first lines
hold the paths to your folders and programs, as shown in the image below, which you
will set in the next section. The paths in the image are examples from an earlier
version of BayesTraits and R, so yours will be different.\
\
```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/windows_shell_project_script.png", dpi = 300)
```
\
\

# Running the Windows PowerShell script 

As in Unix, you always start the analysis from the __project folder__, and the main
PowerShell script moves to the BayesTraits folder by itself. You may also want to find
[further information on how to use Windows PowerShell](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.security/set-executionpolicy?view=powershell-7.2).\

## Editing the project files

__1.__ In the main PowerShell script __BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1__,
set __\$PROJECTFOLDER__ to the path of the project folder, and __\$BAYESTRFOLDER__ to
the path of the __folder__ that contains the BayesTraits executable file. Also set the
paths to the Rscript, Adobe Acrobat, and Microsoft Word executable files in __\$RFOLDER__,
__\$ACROBATFOLDER__, and __\$WORDFOLDER__;\

__2.__ In the R script __2_producing_BayesTraits_phyreg_shell.R__, set `BayesTraits_dir`
to the same path as __\$BAYESTRFOLDER__, and `BayesTraits_exe` to the name of the
executable file, such as `"BayesTraitsV5"`;\

## Running the analysis

__3.__ Open PowerShell as Administrator;\

__4.__ Move to the project folder __BayesTraits_shell_phyreg_project__, i.e. the same
where you should have the main PowerShell script __BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1__;\

__5.__ Execute the following line and choose option __[Y]Yes__;\
__Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine__

__6.__ Execute the following line:\
__Unblock-File -Path .\\BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1__

__7.__ Then perform the full R and BayesTraits run using the PowerShell script by executing the following line:\
__.\\BayesTraits_full_phyreg_shell_windows.ps1__
